heading: INT. MUSEUM OF CLOCKS - GREAT HALL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MUSEUM OF CLOCKS - GREAT HALL - NIGHT
A hundred timepieces, each telling a different hour.
Grandfather cases line the walls like sentries.
Pendulums swing out of rhythm, ticks overlapping in a thin, endless rain.
At the center, under a glass dome, a gilded astronomical clock the size of a carriage glitters, its planets frozen mid-orbit.
Five minutes to midnight.
The building is dark, sleeping.
In the shadow of a long-case clock, four figures crouch like cats.
SERAPHINA VOSS, 40s, in black from throat to ankle, headlamp dimmed to a red coin, leads.
At her shoulder, BARTHOLOMEW QUILL, 60s, silk scarf, gloved fingers unscrewing the cover plate of a wall panel.
KENJI AOKI, 20s, in a catering uniform with a pocketed screwdriver, carries a coil of fiber cable.
DESPINA ARVANITIS, 30s, enormous eyes, a stethoscope hanging from her neck, taps a glass case with the delicacy of a safecracker.
A small radio crackles from Seraphina's belt.
Guard's on the east stairs. Two minutes.
units.name: LOOKOUT

units.text: Understood.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Panel's open.
units.name: BARTHOLOMEW

units.text: Wires are color-coded.
units.name: KENJI

units.text: Ignore the colors. Follow the dust.
units.name: BARTHOLOMEW

units.text: Why?
units.name: KENJI

units.text: The ones that move are the ones they trust.
units.name: BARTHOLOMEW

units.text: Kenji nods.
Pinches a wire.
Clips it.
Seraphina. The dome has a second lock.
units.name: DESPINA

units.text: Meaning?
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Meaning it listens.
units.name: DESPINA

units.text: She presses the stethoscope to the glass.
Closes her eyes.
Her whole body bends toward the sound.
Tick, tick, tick, tick.
It's counting. Three seconds to a click.
units.name: DESPINA

units.text: Can you match it?
units.name: BARTHOLOMEW

units.text: I can try.
units.name: DESPINA

units.text: She slides a slim tool beneath the dome's rim.
Waits.
A pendulum on the east wall swings out.
Another answers.
Tick.
Click.
A pin falls.
One minute. He's at the landing.
units.name: LOOKOUT

units.text: Go.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Despina lifts the dome.
Slow, trembling.
It rises on invisible springs, a hush of glass.
The planets of the clock gleam, close enough to touch.
Kenji slides a velvet bag under the gilded sun and eases it free.
The gears whisper once.
Then still.
It's heavier than it looks.
units.name: BARTHOLOMEW

units.text: They always are.
units.name: KENJI

units.text: Thirty seconds!
units.name: LOOKOUT

units.text: Seal it. Back to the wall.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: They snap the dome back down.
The pin settles.
The clock gleams behind its glass, minus one small golden sun.
Somewhere in the hall, a bell tolls.
Midnight.
Every clock in the museum begins to strike, a hundred chimes, a hundred hours, clamor and swell.
The four crouch, hands over ears, as the hall rings around them like a cathedral.
The guard's footsteps, if any, are drowned entirely.
That's the best alarm I ever heard!
units.name: KENJI

units.text: Quiet!
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: The last chime fades.
Silence, then a single tick, then a hundred.
He's gone to the west wing. You're clear.
units.name: LOOKOUT

units.text: Bartholomew exhales.
Despina leans on the long-case clock, trembling and grinning.
Kenji laughs without sound.
Seraphina lets go of the radio.
Walk. Don't run. Let's go home.
units.name: SERAPHINA
